operational_observations.evidence: PRISMA states it offers AggregateEU on behalf of DG ENER as service provider pursuant to Article 43 of Regulation 2024/1789, and defines AggregateEU as services implementing Articles 42-51.
Commission reports the second 2025 mid-term AggregateEU round and says the permanent joint-purchasing instrument is being established under the Hydrogen and Decarbonised Gases package.

operational_observations.visible_service_name: EU Energy and Raw Materials Platform
operational_observations.legal_basis: Multiple mechanisms and legal mandates, including Regulation (EU) 2024/1789
operational_observations.evidence: Commission launches a broader platform covering hydrogen, raw materials, natural gas and biomethane.

finding.statement: AggregateEU is a counterexample to using visible service/brand continuity as proof of legal-regime identity. The temporary emergency legal regime ended, the permanent successor began without a substantive gap, and the AggregateEU service name continued for a time under the successor legal basis before a broader platform shell launched.

forbidden_inferences: AggregateEU in March 2025 was still operating under Regulation 2022/2576 merely because the brand name was unchanged.
The August 2024 preparatory provisions mean the permanent substantive mechanism overlapped the temporary regime in full.
The EU Energy and Raw Materials Platform is legally identical to AggregateEU or to the gas demand-aggregation regime.
Permanent regime succession proves that every operational feature, service-provider implementation, or IT system remained unchanged.
A continuous visible service proves one continuous legal instrument.
